text:
tara.k: Heads up — nightly evals for `redwood/gptx-13b` showed a huge drop in BLEU and several prompt failures starting at the 02:00 run.

sanjay.m: saw the alert too. which eval set?

tara.k: `wiki-faq-100` and `summ-qa-50`. Failures are mostly weird truncation and repetitive tokens, not hallucinations per se.

jamal: 02:00 corresponds to the microkernel reorder PR landing (runtime/attn: reorder microkernel loops to improve cache). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/8421

marie-runs: CI/bench shows a 1.8% drop in corpus BLEU and a 12% increase in token-level repetition score for that model after the change. Attached logs: `nightly-eval/2026-03-20/13:00/logs.txt` (CI artifact).

tara.k: can someone repro locally with the nightly model snapshot and the same seed? I want to see if it's deterministic.

jamal: repro steps I used:
```
git checkout 3a4f9b2  # PR merge commit
make -C runtime build-attn-microkernel
python eval/run_eval.py --model redwood/gptx-13b --promptset wiki-faq-100 --seed 42 --streaming False
```
My local run shows the same truncation on ~10% of prompts.

sanjay.m: interestingly, if I revert just the loop order in `src/attn/microkernel.cc` the outputs match baseline. Patch region:
```diff
- for (int k=0; k<K; ++k) { for (int i=0; i<I; ++i) { ... }}
+ for (int i=0; i<I; ++i) { for (int k=0; k<K; ++k) { ... }}
```
That reorder reduces cache misses but apparently affects floating sums order and downstream softmax sampling when quantized.

marie-runs: model is running in q4f16 (post-quant) in nightly; quant noise could amplify reorder effects. We saw similar sensitivity in q3 experiments last year.

tara.k: would like a quick bisect to confirm it's this PR and not something else bundled. @ci-bot can you trigger an A/B nightly with and without the microkernel reorder on the same snapshot?

ci-bot: @tara.k Started A/B nightly: group A (baseline) vs group B (with microkernel reorder). Results ETA ~ 35m. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/ab/2026-03-20/1798765432

jamal: meanwhile, I dumped the attention logits for a failing prompt. Diff shows tiny shifts in the top-k probabilities leading to a different token selected at step 12, which cascades into repetition. Small early sample difference explodes.

sanjay.m: that matches a sampling tie-breaker sensitivity. We should check RNG seeding and any introduced nondeterminism in the new loop (e.g., accumulation order).

marie-runs: attaching snippet of the logits around the divergence:
```
step 11 top5 probs baseline: [0.31,0.20,0.12,0.10,0.09]
step 11 top5 probs reordered: [0.30,0.21,0.12,0.10,0.09]
```
seed is same; sampling uses top-p 0.95 + temperature 0.9. small shift changed sampled token.

tara.k: action plan: 1) revert microkernel reorder in prod nightlies for now, 2) add a deterministic float accumulation path for quantized runtimes OR run higher-precision accumulate when quantized, 3) add a small eval that exercises sampling sensitivity after kernel changes.

jamal: agree. I can open hotfix PR to revert the reorder and a follow-up to add an #ifdef for deterministic accumulation in q4 paths.

sanjay.m: also let's add a regression test that runs a few seeds on `wiki-faq-100` and flags >1% BLEU drop or >5% repetition increase. Prevents regressions like this slipping by.

marie-runs: FYI A/B finished: group B (with reorder) shows the same degradation across 6 different models (not just gptx-13b) but magnitude varies. CI report: https://ci.internal/reports/ab/1798765432/results.html

ci-bot: @jamal Hotfix PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/8434 — revert microkernel reorder. Running quick patch build.

tara.k: thanks. Once hotfix lands, let's re-run nightly evaluation and confirm metrics, then plan a careful numerical analysis of accumulation ordering and whether we can use compensated summation (Kahan) in the hot loop.

jamal: will also run localized microbench comparing throughput impact: revert costs ~2.7% perf on long sequences. Need to see if compensated summation costs are acceptable.

sanjay.m: please tag me on the follow-up PR; I can help design the quant-aware accumulation option.

marie-runs: logging note — add a tiny provenance header to nightly artifacts that records runtime git commit + kernel flags so we can trace these faster next time.

tara.k: agreed. Good catch everyone. We'll monitor. :thumbsup:
